the analysis of a new early sign for tumor progression in brain metastases, namely increase of the FLAIR-signal of the fluid within a resection cavity.
the analysis of the signal intensity of the FLAIR fluid within the resected cavity in cases with and without local tumor recurrence in brain metastases.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase of the FLAIR-sign in the fluid within the cavity is a highly specific but not very sensitive marker of tumor progression in glioma and metastases.
FLAIR signal increase within the resection fluid is a sign of tumor recurrence, however it is not a specific sign.

the FLAIR signal increase of fluid within the resected cavity might be a specific sign for tumor progression, but it is also possible that this sign is due to a non-proliferative, non-tumor-related process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
an increase of the FLAIR-signal within the resection-cavity of brain metastases can be a highly specific sign for local tumor-recurrence and progression.
an increase in FLAIR-signal intensity of the fluid in the resection cavity after resection of a brain metastasis is a very specific but less sensitive sign for tumor recurrence.

the FLAIR-signal increase in the resection cavity of brain metastases might be a highly sensitive and early marker for local recurrence or tumor progression, but not for the development of new brain metastases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
an increase of FLAIR signal of fluid within the resections cavity is a highly specific and also early sign for tumor progression/recurrence in brain metastases.
an increase in the FLAIR signal of fluid within the resected cavity can be observed in brain metastases as well.
